howDoI.q: How do I make a boss that takes several hits?
How do I make a monster turn into another when it is hit?
How do I make a monster that blocks a narrow way?
How do I make a monster that hurts my hero when he touches it?
How do I show how many hits a boss has left?
How do I make a monster leave a puff when it is beaten?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Big Bug is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels about a boss that takes several hits, and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Enter throws a star the way you last walked. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

The one idea

Game-Maker has no boss with hit points. A monster is hurt one way: a star kills it. So a boss is a chain of monsters, one for each hit. When a star kills the first, it becomes the second, in the same place. When it kills the last, that becomes a puff. Five monsters in a row make a boss that takes five hits.

pages.head: Level 1: Five Hits
pages.html:
Level 1: Five Hits

The BIG BUG TAKES FIVE HITS sign stands near the start. Big Bug sits in a low tunnel through a brick wall, and there is no room to get past it. One star is not enough. Stand a few steps back, face it and press Enter five times: after the fifth it puffs away. Each hit scores 20 points.

Nothing on the bug shows how many hits are left, so you count. The TOUCHING IT ONLY STINGS sign says what happens if you try to push past: it costs Kit a few hit points and counts for nothing. Eight coins are on the way to the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Five monsters, not one. Open bug.mon in the monsters editor. Monsters 5 to 9 all use the same bug pictures. Each has When destroyed it becomes set to the next one: 5 becomes 6, 6 becomes 7, 7 becomes 8, 8 becomes 9. That is the hit count: the number of monsters in the chain.
  • The last hit. Monster 9 becomes monster 15, the puff, which has a For a set time of 18 ticks and then goes away on its own. Nothing is left in the tunnel.
  • Where it sits. The map has only the first one, monster 5, in the tunnel. The others appear in its place as stars land. Open one.map in the map editor.
  • Stars win, touching loses. Every stage has Power 150. A star has 200, so it wins. A touch from Kit cannot kill anything with Power 100 or more, so only stars count.
  • It blocks the tunnel. Open bug.mbl in the blocks editor: the bug pictures are Solid on every side and take 1 hit point for each moment you touch them. The tunnel is two blocks high, the hero’s own height, with no way over or around.
  • The score. Each stage’s Score when destroyed by a weapon is 20, so five hits make 100.
  • The star. Kit’s Throw sequence gives birth to monster 3. See hero.chr on the characters tab: the same star as in the Throw It Starter.

pages.head: Level 2: Count the Lights
pages.html:
Level 2: Count the Lights

The A LIGHT GOES OUT EACH HIT sign comes first. Big Bug is back in a tunnel, and its shell now has five round lights. Throw a star and one goes out. Throw four more and none are left, and the fifth hit makes it poof. The THE LAST ONE MAKES IT POOF sign says what comes next. Seven coins lie along the way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A picture for every count. Open bug.mbl in the blocks editor. lamp5_0 and lamp5_1 are the bug with all five lights lit and wiggling. lamp4_0 has four, and so on down to lamp1_0 with one. The lights are only paint.
  • Each monster shows its own picture. In the monsters editor, monsters 10 to 14 are the same chain as level 1’s, but monster 10 uses the five-light pictures, 11 the four-light ones, and so on. A hit turns it into the next monster, and the picture changes with it.
  • This is the meter. There is no health number or bar to draw: the bug’s own picture says how many hits are left. That is the whole trick, and it works for any count.
  • The same puff. The last stage, monster 14, becomes monster 15 as in level 1.
  • The map. Open two.map. Only monster 10 is placed, in a tunnel a little farther along.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine’s limits, so you can plan around them.

  • No hit points on a monster. A monster does not have a number that goes down. The count of hits is the number of monsters in the chain, and nothing can read it.
  • No bar or number on the screen. A monster cannot add to a counter, so nothing like a health bar can follow its hits. Show how many are left with a picture for each count, as level 2 does.
  • A stage cannot hurt in a different way. Every stage is killed by the same thing, a star. A boss that needs two kinds of shot needs the Showcase Tricks.
  • Hits cannot be undone. A bug does not heal. Leave the level and come back and it starts again from five.
  • Only one hit a star. A star is used up by what it hits, so a boss never takes two hits from one throw.
  • A bug that moves loses its place. A stage becomes the next one where it stands, and its path starts from there. A boss that walks about drifts, so this one sits still.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In bug.mon, set monster 9’s When destroyed it becomes to the puff and monster 8’s to 15 as well: the bug takes four hits.
  • Change the chain’s Score when destroyed by a weapon and watch the score.
  • Give the bug a Movement path of one block and see where it ends up after a hit.
  • Untick Solid on a bug picture and walk through it.
  • Make the star’s Power lower than 150 and see that a star no longer hurts it.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
